title: China Naps After Lunch — Genius Habit, or Just Slacking? | China Travel Expert
description:
Across China, lunch is often followed by a built-in nap. In many offices the lights go down so people can rest right at their desks — a habit most learned as kids, back in school after lunch. It's called wǔxiū (wǔ xiū), the "midday rest." Think of it as a built-in siesta; sleep science says even a 20-minute nap can sharpen focus. So — genius routine, or just an excuse to sleep at work?

★ Expert Tip: Many small shops, offices and museums in China close for an hour or two right after lunch. Plan errands for mid-morning or later in the afternoon and you'll hit far fewer "back at 2pm" signs.

在中国，午饭后常常有一段「午休」。很多办公室会把灯调暗，大家就趴在桌上小睡——这是很多人从上学时就养成的习惯。它叫午休（wǔ xiū）。你可以把它想成「自带的午睡时间」；研究也说，哪怕 20 分钟的小睡也能让人更专注。那么——这是聪明的习惯，还是上班偷懒的借口？
—
I'm mapping ALL of China — real streets, real history, zero tourist traps.
🧭 Your China Travel Expert | 你的中国旅游专家

Facts verified 2026-11-26:
• A post-lunch midday rest is common in Chinese schools and workplaces; some schools now add lie-flat nap desks, and places like Hangzhou's Qiantang district have set formal "lying-down break" standards — People's Daily https://en.people.cn/n3/2024/0903/c90000-20213924.html + Sixth Tone https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1014494
• China's 2021 Ministry of Education guidance urges schools to protect students' sleep and an adequate lunch break (nap-length rules are set locally) — gov.cn https://english.www.gov.cn/statecouncil/ministries/202104/03/content_WS6067ac56c6d0719374afc027.html + Sixth Tone https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1007136
• A short afternoon nap (~20 min) can boost alertness and focus; much longer naps may bring grogginess — Harvard Health https://www.health.harvard.edu/staying-healthy/can-a-quick-snooze-help-with-energy-and-focus-the-science-behind-power-naps

es.title: China duerme la siesta tras comer — ¿hábito genial o pura pereza?
es.description: En China, tras el almuerzo suele venir una siesta. En muchas oficinas bajan las luces para dormir en el propio escritorio; se llama wǔxiū, el "descanso del mediodía", un hábito aprendido desde la escuela. La ciencia dice que hasta 20 minutos mejoran la concentración. ¿Rutina genial, o excusa para dormir en el trabajo?

pt.title: A China tira soneca após o almoço — hábito genial ou preguiça?
pt.description: Na China, depois do almoço costuma vir uma soneca. Em muitos escritórios as luzes baixam para dormir na própria mesa; chama-se wǔxiū, o "descanso do meio-dia", hábito aprendido desde a escola. A ciência diz que até 20 minutos melhoram o foco. Rotina genial, ou desculpa para dormir no trabalho?

id.title: China tidur siang setelah makan siang — kebiasaan jenius atau malas?
id.description: Di China, setelah makan siang sering ada tidur siang. Di banyak kantor lampu diredupkan agar orang bisa tidur di meja; namanya wǔxiū, "istirahat siang", kebiasaan sejak sekolah. Sains bilang tidur 20 menit saja bisa menajamkan fokus. Rutinitas jenius, atau alasan tidur saat kerja?

hi.title: चीन में दोपहर के खाने के बाद झपकी — बढ़िया आदत या सुस्ती?
hi.description: चीन में दोपहर के भोजन के बाद अक्सर झपकी होती है। कई दफ्तरों में लाइट कम कर दी जाती है ताकि लोग मेज़ पर ही सो सकें; इसे wǔxiū यानी "दोपहर का आराम" कहते हैं, जो स्कूल से सीखी आदत है। विज्ञान कहता है कि 20 मिनट की झपकी भी ध्यान बढ़ाती है। बढ़िया आदत, या काम पर सोने का बहाना?

ar.title: الصين تغفو بعد الغداء — عادة عبقرية أم مجرد تكاسل؟
ar.description: في الصين كثيراً ما تلي الغداءَ قيلولة. في كثير من المكاتب تُخفَّت الأضواء لينام الناس على مكاتبهم؛ تُسمى wǔxiū أي "راحة الظهيرة"، عادة تُكتسب منذ المدرسة. يقول العلم إن قيلولة 20 دقيقة تعزّز التركيز. أهي روتين عبقري، أم ذريعة للنوم في العمل؟

fr.title: La Chine fait la sieste après le déjeuner — géniale habitude ou flemme ?
fr.description: En Chine, le déjeuner est souvent suivi d'une sieste. Dans beaucoup de bureaux, on baisse les lumières pour dormir à même son bureau ; on appelle ça wǔxiū, le "repos de midi", une habitude apprise dès l'école. La science dit que même 20 minutes aiguisent la concentration. Routine géniale, ou prétexte pour dormir au travail ?
